ONE PARSER: a function in src/concordance/verifiers/mathematics.py (no new module, since the closure gate compares module sets) reads an expression text into sympy objects. It normalises the text once, then gives exactly that text to ast.parse in eval mode, then builds the result by walking the tree. The text it parses is the only text; nothing re-reads the input afterwards. It accepts these nodes and refuses every other: Expression; Constant int and float, never str, bytes, None, bool, complex or Ellipsis; Name; BinOp Add, Sub, Mult, Div, Pow, Mod; UnaryOp USub, UAdd; Tuple; Compare where today's claims need it; and Call whose function is a bare Name on _ALLOWED_FUNCS, with keywords only from a short fixed list. A Name resolves to the caller's names, or to a fixed table of constants, or else to Symbol(name); a name beginning with an underscore, an allowlisted function used as a value, and any other name sympy would read as something other than a symbol are refused. So no Name can ever yield a Python object from outside those tables, and no callable can be passed as a value. A value a call returns must be a sympy object or a container of them; a Python str is refused, so nothing can reach a second parse. Integers and decimals become Integer, Float from the digits as written, or Rational under rational=True, as sympify gives today.

BOUNDS: the parser, not a separate pass over a different text, applies today's limits: nodes, depth, the length of the text, the exponent cap, and a cap on the bits of an integer power however its base was built, including powers nested on the base side. The caret spelling is normalised before parsing, so one operator carries one limit. RecursionError and any failure inside the walk become a refusal, never an unhandled error. Compute-heavy allowlisted functions are not capped here beyond today's timeout, and the lead's want note files that.

EVERY CALLER: mathematics' _parse and _domain_mismatch and physics' equation and unit readers all use the parser, and _domain_mismatch reads the same normalised text _parse read, with an unevaluated build equivalent to evaluate=False for pole bases. physics uses it with its symbol names and its unit table as the caller's names. physics' sympify(1) becomes Integer(1). The parser works in a fresh interpreter whichever verifier is imported first. A symbols key must be a plain identifier, or the packet is refused.

A REFUSAL NEVER PASSES: mathematics keeps today's reading of a refused text, NOT_APPLICABLE. In physics, a packet whose equation or unit is refused returns that one NOT_APPLICABLE result and no other, so the step reads INCOMPLETE and a passing check in the same packet cannot lift it to HOLDS, because derivation.py's _status drops NOT_APPLICABLE. A test sends a refused equation beside a passing check and reads INCOMPLETE and no seal. A non-dict or empty symbols reads the same.

SAME READINGS: a differential test reads every expression in the benchmark's packets, the goldens, the check goldens and the derivation tier, plus a fixed table of forms (rationals, decimals, long decimals, tuples for Sum limits, every allowlisted function with a typical argument, every constant), through the parser and through sympy's sympify in the test alone, and the two are structurally equal, with rational=True too; for the unevaluated build it compares pole sets. Each form the parser refuses and sympify accepted is listed by name in the test with its reason. ONE PARSER: a function in src/concordance/verifiers/mathematics.py (no new module, since the closure gate compares module sets) reads an expression text into sympy objects. It normalises the text once, refuses it by _INVALID_EXPR_RE, refuses any text or caller's name that Unicode NFKC would change, since ast normalises identifiers and one name would otherwise become two symbols, then gives exactly that text to ast.parse in eval mode and builds the result by walking the tree. The text it parses is the only text; nothing re-reads the input afterwards. It accepts these nodes and refuses every other: Expression; Constant int and float, never str, bytes, None, bool, complex or Ellipsis; Name; BinOp Add, Sub, Mult, Div, Pow, Mod, on sympy values only, never a tuple or list; UnaryOp USub, UAdd; Tuple, as a call argument at any depth, so a matrix can still be written; Compare where today's claims need it; and Call whose function is a bare Name on _ALLOWED_FUNCS, with no keywords at all, since no moat or tier text uses one. A caller's name used as a function is refused. A Name resolves to the caller's names, or to a fixed table of constants, or else to Symbol(name); a name beginning with an underscore, an allowlisted function used as a value, and any other name sympy would read as something other than a symbol are refused. So no Name can yield a Python object from outside those tables, and no callable can be passed as a value. nsimplify, which parses text it builds inside the call, comes off _ALLOWED_FUNCS and is a listed refused form; nothing uses it. A value a call returns must be a sympy object, or a list, tuple or dict of them checked at every depth; an iterator and a str are refused; a plain int or bool from igcd, ilcm, nextprime, prevprime or isprime becomes Integer or sympy's true or false. That check runs after the call, so it is a second line: what stops a parse inside a call is that no str and no callable can reach one. Integers and decimals become Integer, Float from the digits as written, or Rational under rational=True, as sympify gives today.

BOUNDS: the parser applies every limit to the tree it builds, never to a different text: at most 4,000 characters of text; today's node, depth and exponent limits; and a cap of 2**20 bits on a power, whether written with the operator or with the Pow function, on an integer or rational base, however the base was built, including powers nested on the base side. The caret spelling is normalised before parsing. RecursionError and any failure inside the walk become a refusal, never an unhandled error. A test holds each limit at its edge. findings: src/concordance/verifiers/mathematics.py:198-211 (_bound_power): the 2**20-bit cap is beaten on a case BOUNDS names, powers nested on the base side. It reads only a Rational coefficient, so a base that is an integer or rational raised to a fraction, not a perfect power, has coefficient 1 and passes; sympy then multiplies the exponents out into one integer power as the outer power is built. Measured with scaled inputs, by the operator and the Pow function: an Integer of 3.2 to 9.5 times the cap, reading HOLDS through http_api.route in equality, numeric, calc_chain, a physics equation and a physics unit. A 28-character text of the class stalled the whole process about 10 s, past the 8 s timeout, and the size grows with the base. The floor in steps also lets a fractional exponent reach twice the cap, so the docstring's upper bound is false. No test row holds this class. Fix: bound the base's own base and exponent over every factor, with a ceiling and not a floor, and add rows at the edge.

src/concordance/verifiers/mathematics.py:299-305 (_Reader._binop, unevaluated build): EVERY CALLER's 'equivalent to evaluate=False for pole bases' fails. sympy's transformer flattens nested Add and Mul; this build keeps the nesting, so two sides that differ only in the right-nesting of a sum or a product inside a denominator get pole sets that compare different. A true identity then moves from HOLDS at base to BROKEN, with a detail saying it holds only off a singular set. Measured through the route on one generated set of 2,418 claims, run at base and on this code: 321 changed, all HOLDS to BROKEN, none toward HOLDS. So it is no false positive, but it is a changed reading SAME READINGS does not permit, and the differential's corpus and table hold no right-nested pole. Fix: flatten in the unevaluated build as sympy does, and add such pairs to the table, compared by pole sets and by verdict.

src/concordance/verifiers/physics.py:130-131 and src/concordance/verifiers/mathematics.py:1058: a value the parser read alone is substituted into a power after the parser, so no limit sees the power. A unit in symbols or a claimed_solution value, inside every limit by itself, put into a power over a symbol builds an integer past the cap and past the exponent limit, with its size set by the request. Measured scaled at about 9.5 times the cap, and the physics packet read HOLDS. It is the same at base, and BOUNDS' wording binds the parser's tree, but these are request fields and the compute class stays open by one hop on the path this run exists to close. Fix: apply _bound_power to each power with the substituted values, in one shared helper, before .subs; or the lead rules it out of this run in a plan note and files a want.

findings: src/concordance/verifiers/mathematics.py:232-243 with :383-389: 'an unevaluated read multiplies nothing' is false, so the cap is skipped on a read that multiplies. The Pow function is not in _UNEVALUATED_FUNCS, so in _domain_mismatch's read it still evaluates, with multiplied False. A base that collapses to a small value in the evaluated read, so the cap passes there, stays whole in the unevaluated read and is multiplied out. BOUNDS names the Pow function. Measured: peak memory 51 times the cap on a scaled input, and a 30-character text of the class read HOLDS through http_api.route after 14.9 s with a 7.7 s stall of every thread; the size grows with the base. simplify and Integer around the operator multiply in that read too. Fix: make that read of a Pow call multiply nothing, or bound it, and pin the function form in test_an_unevaluated_read_multiplies_nothing. Do not simply refuse there: _domain_mismatch reads a failed read as no mismatch, so a refusal in that read hides a pole and makes a new false positive.

src/concordance/verifiers/mathematics.py:215-216 (_power_bits): the walk is default-allow, so a carrier it does not know counts 0 bits and the cap passes. A scan of all 147 allowlisted functions in 17 shapes, 2,499 rows, by both spellings and with the result size measured, found carriers besides Piecewise and matrices. By the operator, a Poly returns a coefficient past the cap (7 shapes, one of them a constant polynomial, which is an integer by another name), and the matrix expressions Transpose, Inverse and a root of a matrix multiply out through MatPow.doit (6 shapes). Measured at 1.4 to 2.9 times the cap on scaled inputs. It is finding 1's class by another carrier, and its effect grows with the base the same way. Fix: make the walk default-deny, for example count every Rational in any base it cannot walk, or refuse a numeric power on one, and add a row per carrier at the edge.

text: ROTATION (lead), on the owner's word in chat, 2026-11-04: 'Yeah. Rotate if you can.' The V3 issuer key was rotated at 2026-11-04T15:34:59Z with the project's own keygen, the secret never printed: kid ed25519:707bb45bf5773554 retired, kid ed25519:d198c25edae9e641 current. Before rotating, all 3 seals were settled, so none could be re-signed or published by a read. After it, the /s/<hash>?html=1 page of each seal has the sha256 it had before, /ledger/verify reads 3 of 3, and each seal's envelope and in_toto attestation keep the old kid. So /capabilities' transparency kid differs from the live-before note at line 10 for this reason, and a live checker names it as explained. The JSON form of a seal changes on each read: see the want below.

head: 82078d17d7063fd40a830a7daac6585db670f56e
text: CLAIM, round 3 (builder-13), added to the step's claim: the power limits now bind the unevaluated read as well as the evaluated one, so that read can refuse a text the evaluated read took. Such a refusal is not checkable: the equality reads INCOMPLETE, never no mismatch and never HOLDS, so a true claim that read HOLDS at the base can read INCOMPLETE, and no reading moves toward HOLDS. The test test_an_unevaluated_read_takes_what_the_evaluated_read_took and its neighbour test_an_unevaluated_read_multiplies_nothing, both new in this step, pinned an exemption that checker-33's line 24 showed was wrong: a call in that read still multiplies. They are replaced by tests that pin the limits in that read, the function form as well as the operator, and pin that the refusal fails closed. Every other failed read keeps today's reading.

text: RULING (lead) on checker-33's close call in its round 3 report: simplify around a Pow whose exponent a function hides still multiplies past the cap in the unevaluated read. simplify does the multiplying, not the power; plain Pow on that form never multiplies. That is the compute-heavy class the plan leaves to the timeout, and it reaches no evaluation, so it goes to want (2) with the nested fractional chain, and it does not reopen the step. Also filed: the module walk moved behind -m slow, so a new evaluator site is caught only by CI's slow job; move it back to the fast path, at a cost of 1 to 2 s. Nothing pins the equality edge at half the cap, and _bound_power's docstring overclaims for a hidden exponent.
